sentences.text: Reesodus was an extinct genus of hybodontiform fish, a group belonging to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous relatives of modern sharks and rays.
The teeth of the type species, Reesodus underwoodi, are notably small, symmetrical, and measure between 0.4 and 0.5 mm in height.
The genus name honors Jan Rees, the first scientist to recognize these fossils as belonging to a distinct genus.
The defining species, Reesodus underwoodi, was described from the Khuff Formation of Oman.
The genus was formally established in 2013 as a replacement name for the previously unnamed 'Palaeozoic Genus 2'.
Fossil remains have been found in England, Russia, and Oman.

It is classified as Hybodontiformes incertae sedis because its heterodonty pattern and potential enlarged lateral teeth cannot be assessed, though it is assumed to be close to the family Lonchidiidae.
Reesodus lived from the Tournaisian age of the Early Carboniferous to the Wordian age of the Permian, spanning from 339.9 to 264.28 million years ago.
